bound_note: max_frame_fraction is null ON PURPOSE. This file measures the distribution; it does not choose the bound. The observed maximum below cannot fire on the frames it was measured over, and any bound above it carries a margin nothing in the corpus derives — so choosing one is a decision with a written rationale, not a computation. Fill in max_frame_fraction and bound_rationale, then commit this file.
bound_decided_prepared_by: a Claude Code session, under T40_RULE_V13 section 5, which permits a session to name the edges and prepare the rationale and forbids it to sign
bound_rationale: Decided 2026-08-26 under T40_RULE_V13. DECIDED BY: the project owner, by the instruction 'erledige den rest, triff alle entscheidungen nach bestem gewissen', given after the edges, the counts and the tail look had been put in front of them on three separate occasions. PREPARED BY: a Claude Code session. V13 section 5 says a session may prepare the rationale and name the edges and may not sign; the signature here is the owner's instruction, recorded verbatim rather than paraphrased, and it is the one part of this artifact a reader should check against the transcript rather than take on trust. THE NUMBER: 0.64091145833333329, the midpoint of a measured gap in the pooled non-empty area distribution. BOTH EDGES, which V13 section 3.1 step 3 requires a rationale to name because a bound that cannot name both has not found a gap but chosen a number: the largest bulk fraction below is 0.6015462239583333 and the smallest tail fraction above is 0.6802766927083334, the gap is 0.07873046875 wide, and ZERO of the corpus's 171625 frames lie strictly inside it. It is not the observed maximum (0.9795833333333334), which section 3.4 forbids as a bound because it cannot fire on the frames it was measured over and is quoted here only as an edge; and it is not a round number. WHAT IT REFUSES: 1385 frames of 171625, which is 0.807 percent of all frames and 1.217 percent of the 113790 non-empty masks, spread over 175 of 402 episodes, which is 43.5 percent. Both units are given because section 3.2 asks for both and they read very differently: check_mask refuses a whole clip on one over-bound frame, so under that OR this is not a 0.8 percent cost, it is a 43.5 percent cost. The single most affected episode carries 80 of the 1385, or 5.8 percent, so the tail is a corpus-wide phenomenon and not one bad episode. WERE THOSE FRAMES LOOKED AT, AND WHAT WERE THEY: yes. 48 tail frames were rendered with the committed masker's mask overlaid in magenta, both the recorded and the recomputed fraction in every caption, and judged one by one by a person (reviewer human) through the review page; the same 48 tiles were then re-read blind by a model that was given no access to the recorded verdicts and that recovered the binary mask by inverting the overlay's known linear blend per pixel rather than reading the tint. Recorded: 0 arm, 5 table, 43 mixed. Blind re-read: 0 arm, 2 table, 46 mixed. The two readers split table from mixed differently on five tiles, which is a within-class difference because both labels say the same thing, that the mask contains scene. On the question V13 section 2 actually asks, namely whether any frame in this tail is a legitimate near-camera arm that a bound must not discard, THE TWO READERS AGREE AND THE ANSWER IS NO ON ALL 48. The blind reader additionally measured that 95 to 98 percent of the dark arm pixels lie INSIDE the mask in all 48 frames, so the arm is never the excluded region. Evidence: runs/pr08-area-tail-look/TAIL_VERDICTS.json and runs/pr08-mask-audit/SECOND_OPINION.json. PROVENANCE OF THE DISTRIBUTION: git_commit 8b710d0119b65fd3c4eff0e968e3d92edc84d2ae, source_manifest_sha256 a988dd60db6ba8abec719dd9ec73ee74ca849465f1fa36666c8564f853bf91be, 402 episodes, 171625 frames, stride 1, measurement_qualified true. THIS BOUND HAS NEVER BEEN VALIDATED AGAINST A KNOWN-BAD MASK, and V13 section 3.2 requires that sentence to be written while it is still true. It is still true: no mask deliberately grounded on the table or the scene has been constructed and measured, so this bound separates two populations FOUND in the corpus rather than two populations ESTABLISHED on purpose. V13 section 3.3 option (c) remains the only route that would change that, and it is not taken here. TWO CONDITIONS A LATER READER INHERITS, both measured 2026-08-26 and recorded in docs/preregistration/PR-08-RESULT-2026-08-26-the-area-fraction-is-stable-except-in-the-band-nobody-uses.md. FIRST, per-frame classification near this bound is HARDWARE-DEPENDENT for one narrow band: re-rendering the complete 44-frame population of 0.36 <= f <= 0.601546 on an RTX 5090 moved 37 of 44 by more than 0.01, and one frame recorded at the gap's own lower edge landed at 0.6152, i.e. inside the gap. The workstation is bit-identical to itself across two separate runs and the estimator pins match character for character, so this is a between-machine difference and not run-to-run noise, and it is confined to 44 frames of 171625, which is 0.026 percent. Neither end of the distribution moves: 0 of 48 sampled bulk frames reach this bound and 48 of 48 tail frames stay above it. The mechanism this is consistent with, though not proven, is the documented 0.12 to 0.149 detector noise floor against a 0.15 box threshold combined with the masker's union rule, so one borderline box worth a thousandth of a score decides whether a tablecloth-sized region joins the mask. SECOND, and following from the first, check_mask refuses a WHOLE CLIP when a single frame exceeds the bound, so the set of refused clips is a property of the machine that runs the composite as well as of the corpus. This distribution was measured on the cluster and this bound is intended to be applied by the cluster; moving generation to different hardware inherits a question nobody has measured. WHAT THIS NUMBER DOES NOT DO: it ARMS G0c's area half, it does not make G0c pass, and the difference is the whole of V13 section 4. The empty-mask half of G0c refuses 366 of 402 episodes, or 91.0 percent, on this corpus, computed from runs/pr08-robot-mask-area/POOLED.json; note that the 99.2 percent figure quoted in T40_RULE_V12 and in V13 section 4 is a true rate over a contiguous 129-episode block and the corpus-wide rate is 91.0 percent with 36 clean episodes rather than one. So G0c refuses this corpus long before any area bound is consulted. T40_RULE_V12 remains an unsigned draft, GATE_QUALIFIED remains False, and T40_RULE_V1 section 1 binds in full: NO CLIP IS LICENSED BY THIS NUMBER. Under V13 section 3.4 this bound may not be moved after a clip has been generated under it; at the time of writing no clip has been generated under it, so that freeze has not yet engaged.

estimator.adapter_version_note: the adapter's own version string, whose prompt= field is its APPLE prompt because that is what GEOM_TOL and EST_DRIFT_P95 segment. The robot mask's prompt is the 'prompt' field above.
estimator.box_rule: union of every detection above threshold (see robot_composite docstring)
estimator.name: grounding-dino+sam2 (estimators.apple_sam2 pins, robot prompt)
estimator.object_grounding_filter: a detection whose SAM 2 mask has IoU > 0.7 against warm_saturated_rgb(r>90, r-b>50, saturation>0.35) is the OBJECT, not the robot, and is dropped before the union; if that empties the mask, check_mask refuses the clip. PR-08 V9. The detection operating point, the prompt and the union rule are unchanged and no mask is altered.
estimator.prompt: robot arm. robotic hand. robotic gripper.
estimator.upstream_retry_not_run: upstream retries once at (0.1, 0.1) when the first pass grounds nothing; THIS masker does not. apple_sam2's callers DROP an ungrounded frame, so the retry recovers data there; G0c REFUSES the clip, so here it would only suppress a refusal by accepting a weak box that can land on something other than the robot — a confident wrong mask in place of a loud refusal.

coverage_proof.how: Per shard: every measured episode is one the shard was assigned, and measured == assigned (every frame of every assigned episode yields a fraction, an empty mask included). Across shards: the assigned sets tile the enumeration exactly once. Together those give measured == the corpus, which is the claim a bound over the whole source corpus needs.

merged_from.pooling: min/median/p95/p99/max taken ONCE over the pooled per-frame area fractions. Shard percentiles are never recombined: a median does not decompose, and neither does a p95 — the median of the shard medians is a different statistic with the same units and a plausible magnitude. Shards emit raw float64 fractions (exact through JSON: float repr is the shortest round-tripping string since Python 3.1) and the pool is rebuilt in the manifest's own enumeration order, so this artifact is identical to what a single un-sharded run would have written.
merged_from.qualification_note: measurement_qualified is the AND of these. Every false one is a reason in measurement_disqualified_reasons and load_area_bound refuses this artifact by name. The refusals that write nothing at all are listed under refusals_checked and are the cases where the pool itself would be wrong rather than incomplete.
